extracted.intended_audience: company preparers of sustainability disclosures (corporate reporting, finance and sustainability teams), CFOs and sustainability leads
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing corporate sustainability (including climate) disclosures in line with the ISSB’s IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 standards, and practical steps companies should take to be ready for reporting. Focuses on what to disclose (material risks/opportunities, strategy, metrics) and how to prepare organisationally and operationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose material sustainability-related risks and opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose all information about sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect a company’s prospects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as the main objective of IFRS S1 — disclosures should be material (investor-focused) and centred on risks/opportunities that affect company prospects. Use this objective as the primary filter for inclusion and to define materiality thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include sustainability disclosures with the financial statements to meet investor needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires disclosure of material information about sustainability-related risks and opportunities with the financial statements, to meet investor information needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustainability disclosures are intended to accompany and inform the financial statements; preparers should align reporting timelines and ensure the disclosures supply the information investors need to assess enterprise value and future prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide industry-specific disclosures (use SASB guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires industry specific disclosures and refers to the industry-based SASB standards for guidance when identifying disclosures about sustainability-related risks or opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where relevant, use SASB/industry-based metrics and disclosures to capture sector-specific risks and performance. Industry guidance helps identify the most decision‑useful disclosures and avoids generic or irrelevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable investors to understand links between sustainability information and financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires disclosures that enable investors to understand the connections between the sustainability-related risks and opportunities and the sustainability-related financial disclosures and financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit how sustainability risks/opportunities translate into financial impacts (e.g., cash flows, assets, liabilities, valuation). Narrative and quantitative links are both important; avoid siloed reporting that fails to show financial consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards are GAAP agnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: IFRS S1 (and S2) are GAAP agnostic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Standards are not prescriptive about which GAAP a company uses for financial reporting; focus on meeting the sustainability disclosure requirements regardless of underlying accounting framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply IFRS S1 and S2 together
rubrics_metrics.description: The two Standards are designed to be applied together; IFRS S2 captures climate-specific requirements while S1 sets general sustainability disclosure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use S1 as the general disclosure framework and apply S2 for climate-related matters. Treat the Standards as complementary: S1’s materiality and linkage requirements plus S2’s climate-specific metrics and scenario guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy disclosures must distinguish physical and transition risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy disclosures that distinguish between physical and transitional risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing strategy and resilience, explicitly separate and explain physical climate risks (e.g., extreme weather, chronic changes) from transition risks (e.g., policy, market, technological changes), and how each affects strategy and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose plans to respond to climate-related risks and opportunities, including target-setting and legal/regulatory targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of their plans to respond to climate-related risks and opportunities, including how climate-related targets are set and any targets it is required to meet by law or regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain response plans, governance around target-setting, the rationale and methodology for targets, and any regulatory or legal obligations to meet particular targets. Be explicit about which targets are voluntary versus legally mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform scenario analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should perform scenario analysis to explain how various climate-related events may impact the business in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scenario analysis to illustrate potential future states and impacts under different climate trajectories; disclose assumptions, time horizons, key variables, and sensitivity of outcomes. Scenario disclosure should inform strategic decision-making and investor assessment of resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report cross-industry climate metrics (e.g., greenhouse gas emissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related metrics and target disclosures should include cross-industry metrics that are relevant to all companies e.g. greenhouse gas emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include standard, comparable metrics such as GHG emissions (scope 1, 2 and 3 where relevant). Ensure metrics are clearly defined, measured consistently, and accompanied by methodology, boundaries, and any estimates or exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report industry-based climate metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related metrics and target disclosures should include industry-based metrics relevant to companies within the related industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement cross-industry metrics with sector-specific indicators (as per SASB or other industry guidance) that capture material issues for the company’s industry to increase comparability and decision-usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report company-specific metrics used by board/management
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related metrics and target disclosures should include company specific metrics considered by the board or management when measuring progress towards set targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose bespoke internal KPIs that the board/management use to track performance against sustainability targets, including definitions, governance, frequency of review, and how these metrics drive management decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: prepare to report concurrently with financial statements; check local exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared for the possibility of reporting on 2024 information – remember the sustainability report will have to be reported on at the same time as your financial statements (the ISSB exemption noted above may be allowed for the first reporting period, but is dependent upon local jurisdictions and regulators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan year‑end processes to integrate sustainability reporting with financial close. Check for any jurisdictional transition/exemption rules from the ISSB and local regulators that might affect first-year timing and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate current governance and sustainability strategy; perform gap analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate your current governance structure and sustainability strategy to ensure it is fit for purpose going forwards and perform gap analysis to identify areas where work is needed to enable compliance with the Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess board and management oversight, roles/responsibilities, existing policies, reporting lines and capability. Conduct a gap analysis against S1/S2 requirements to prioritise workstreams and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a sustainability roadmap with milestones, responsibilities and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: After understanding your current position, establish how you can address the gaps identified, adopting a timeline of key milestones for your sustainability journey, identifying individuals within your organisation responsible and any potential constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a project plan that assigns owners, sets realistic milestones, allocates resources, identifies dependencies and constraints, and includes checkpoints to monitor progress toward compliance and quality disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure good quality sustainability data with adequate controls and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure adequate controls and processes are in place now to help collate and analyse good quality sustainability data that will complement your disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement data governance, internal controls, data collection procedures, validation and audit trails. Invest in systems/processes to improve accuracy, completeness and timeliness of sustainability data used in disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarise with the Standards to avoid duplication or omission
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarise yourself with the Standards — companies who are already reporting on sustainability information will likely have an advantage but it’s important to note there will be some differences in the Standards which you will need to identify. Not having a good understanding of all the applicable standards could result in lengthy reports containing duplication or omitted information resulting in non-compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map existing reporting frameworks and disclosures to IFRS S1/S2, identify overlaps and gaps, and update reporting templates and governance to prevent duplication or omission. Train reporting teams on the specific expectations of the Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate the organisation and secure top-level buy-in
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all levels of your business have a sound understanding on the importance of sustainability to help drive, grow and implement your sustainability strategy, ensuring there is buy-in at the top of your organisation to encourage the correct mindset to filter down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run awareness and training programmes, involve senior leadership in target-setting and oversight, and communicate the strategic importance of sustainability reporting across functions to ensure coordinated implementation and cultural alignment.
